verdicts.claim: By default SQLite checkpoints automatically on a COMMIT that leaves the WAL at 1000 pages or more. The threshold is set by wal_aut
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more'; pragma.html: 'zero or a negative value turns auto-checkpointing off ... interval of 1000 or SQLITE_DEFAULT_WAL_AUTOCHECKPOINT'

verdicts.claim: Every automatic checkpoint is PASSIVE. PASSIVE copies as many frames as it can without waiting ... busy-handler callback is never invoked
verdicts.evidence: pragma.html: 'All automatic checkpoints are PASSIVE.'; c3ref: 'The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode.'

verdicts.claim: A checkpoint cannot copy past the end mark of any active reader ... records its position in the wal-index and resumes
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'must stop when it reaches a page in the WAL that is past the end mark of any current reader ... remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got'

verdicts.claim: The WAL file resets to the start only when the checkpoint has moved every frame into the database, the database is synced, and no
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL'

verdicts.claim: A PASSIVE checkpoint does not shrink the -wal file on disk, so the file keeps its high-water size.
verdicts.evidence: litestream: 'a passive restart does not truncate the physical -wal file, the file retains its high-water size on disk'; wal.html: 'does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set)'

verdicts.claim: FULL checkpoints block until no writer is active and all readers use the latest snapshot. RESTART adds a wait ... TRUNCATE ... zero bytes
verdicts.evidence: c3ref: FULL 'blocks ... until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot'; TRUNCATE 'truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return'

verdicts.claim: If the WAL keeps overlapping readers, no checkpoint can finish and the WAL grows without bound. The SQLite docs suggest scheduling
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound. This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are "reader gaps"'

verdicts.claim: A read transaction left open for hours blocks removal of every WAL page written after it started. A Syncthing team reported this
verdicts.evidence: syncthing (2026-02-06): 'If a transaction is open for hours, we can't remove pages written to the WAL after its start ... our application level checkpointer is timer based, we might never hit a timewindow without an active reader' (source says 'transaction', draft narrows to 'read transaction')

verdicts.claim: Disagreement: The WAL page says RESTART and TRUNCATE checkpoints may block readers while they run. The PRAGMA page says RESTART
verdicts.evidence: wal.html: 'readers might block while the checkpoint is running'; pragma.html: 'RESTART blocks concurrent writers while it is running, but allows readers to proceed.'

verdicts.claim: PASSIVE never resets or shrinks the WAL file.
verdicts.evidence: litestream: 'Litestream first attempts a PASSIVE checkpoint. If that restarts the WAL and brings the synced offset back below the threshold...'; wal.html: auto (PASSIVE) checkpoint runs 'and the WAL file is recycled' — 'shrinks' holds, 'never resets' does not (uncited Overview sentence)
